- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.33 or below) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a recent spike in price, model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; cap forecast peak at 1–2% above recent high or adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.00–0.11), model tends to overestimate near-term decline; apply slight downward bias to early forecast days.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early days of forecast horizon (e.g., day 1–3) when sentiment is positive; add 0.5–1.5% to initial forecast values.
- When sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings (e.g., 0.00–0.06), model tends to ignore trend; apply slight upward bias to forecast mid-range.
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome by 1–2% across 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 3–5 days to align with mean reversion.
- For horizon > 10 days, model often overestimates volatility; reduce forecast variance by 10–20% if sentiment is flat or mildly negative.
